questions.q: What do we call frozen water?
questions.fact: Ice is water that got so cold it turned solid.

questions.q: What do magnets stick to?
questions.fact: Every magnet has two ends, called poles.

questions.q: What do we hear with?
questions.fact: Sound travels in waves that your ears catch.

questions.q: What color do you get when you mix blue and yellow paint?
questions.fact: Mixing colors makes new colors.

questions.q: What pulls things down to the ground?
questions.fact: Gravity is why a ball comes back down when you throw it up.

questions.q: What do your lungs help you do?
questions.fact: You breathe in and out about 20,000 times each day.

questions.q: Which of these is a solid?
questions.fact: Solids keep their own shape.

questions.q: What turns an ice cube back into water?
questions.fact: When ice gets warm enough, it melts into water.

questions.q: What do plants drink?
questions.fact: Plants take in water through their roots.

questions.q: Which of these can you see through?
questions.fact: Light passes right through clear glass.

questions.q: What is a big spark of electricity in a storm cloud called?
questions.fact: Lightning is much hotter than the surface of the Sun.

questions.q: What is the loud rumble that comes after lightning called?
questions.fact: Thunder is the sound lightning makes as it heats the air.

questions.q: Which of these floats on water?
questions.fact: Things float if they are light for their size.

questions.q: Which body part do you use to smell?
questions.fact: Your nose can tell thousands of different smells apart.

questions.q: What are the three main states of matter?
questions.fact: Water can be all three: ice, liquid water and steam.

questions.q: What force slows down things that slide or rub together?
questions.fact: Rubbing your hands together makes them warm because of friction.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural material?
questions.fact: Diamonds are made of carbon squeezed by heat and pressure deep in Earth.

questions.q: What is the most common gas in the air we breathe?
questions.fact: About one fifth of the air is oxygen.

questions.q: What kind of material lets electricity flow through easily?
questions.fact: Metals like copper are good conductors of electricity.

questions.q: Which of your senses do the tiny hairs deep in your ears help?
questions.fact: Tiny hair cells turn sound into signals for your brain.

questions.q: About how many bones does a grown-up have?
questions.fact: Babies are born with about 300, and some join together as they grow.

questions.q: At what temperature does water boil at sea level, in Celsius?
questions.fact: Water boils at a lower temperature high up on a mountain.

questions.q: What makes a sound?
questions.fact: When a guitar string vibrates, it makes the air wiggle, too.

questions.q: What happens when you push two north poles of magnets together?
questions.fact: Opposite poles attract, and the same poles push apart.

questions.q: What is it called when a liquid turns into a solid?
questions.fact: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, which is 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: What kind of energy do solar panels use?
questions.fact: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.

questions.q: Why do drops appear on the outside of a cold glass on a warm day?
o: Water from the air condenses on it
questions.fact: This is called condensation.

questions.q: What is it called when light bends as it passes through water or glass?
questions.fact: Refraction makes a straw look bent in a glass of water.

questions.q: What is the center of an atom called?
questions.fact: The nucleus holds tiny particles called protons and neutrons.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.fact: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.q: About how fast does light travel?
questions.fact: Nothing we know of travels faster than light.

questions.q: What do plant cells have that animal cells do not?
questions.fact: The cell wall helps a plant stand up straight.

questions.q: What do we call a substance made of only one kind of atom?
questions.fact: Gold, oxygen and iron are all elements.

questions.q: What kind of energy does a moving object have?
questions.fact: A rolling ball has kinetic energy, and a ball held up high has potential energy.

questions.q: Why does the sky look blue in the daytime?
o: Air scatters blue light the most
questions.fact: At sunset, light goes through more air, so the sky looks red and orange.

questions.q: Which of these is a unit for measuring electric current?
questions.fact: Volts tell how hard electricity pushes, and amps tell how much flows.

questions.q: On the pH scale, what is the pH of pure water?
questions.fact: Lemon juice has a pH below 7, and baking soda mixed with water is above 7.

questions.q: What is the hardest part of your body?
questions.fact: Enamel is the shiny outer layer of your teeth.

questions.q: Why can sound not travel through outer space?
questions.fact: Sound needs air or something else to travel through.

questions.q: What is the unit for measuring force?
questions.fact: One newton is about the weight of a small apple.

questions.q: What does a hertz measure?
o: How many cycles happen each second
questions.fact: One hertz is one cycle per second.

questions.q: Which scientist is famous for the theory of gravity and a legend about an apple?
questions.fact: Isaac Newton wrote about gravity in the 1600s.
